# Review, pass 1 — iliad-109 (Iliad 17.106–197)

Method: notes' grammatical labels and cross-references checked against each line; Greek → `l` word by word; `l` ↔ `i`; remembered English; quotation marks, `mark`s, `p` flags and the speech boundary against the last unit of iliad-108 (Menelaus' speech closes with ” at 17.105, so 106 opens in narrative); house table checked by grep. `t` was not touched (verified identical to the pre-edit file and, joined, to the packet's 92 lines). Scansion flags: none in the packet. Reused lines (17.117, 128, 140, 148, 165, 169, 173, 177, 179, 185, 188) compared with the packet: `l`/`i` for the whole-unit repeat at 169 is identical; the others follow the published wording as far as the sentence allows (the one departure, 188 `i`, is fixed below).

## Drafter's uncertainties, adjudicated

- **σπεύσομεν (120–121)**: kept as a hortatory short-vowel subjunctive, "let us hasten", with αἴ κε … προφέρωμεν. A future "we shall hasten" would leave the αἴ κε clause without a purpose to hang on; the note already says "probably".
- **πεφήσεται (155)**: kept "will be shown / will show itself". It needs a subject ὄλεθρος that appears, not one that is slain; the note now says the derivation is uncertain and no longer says "usually".
- **ὄφρ’ ἂν … δύω (186)**: changed to "until" (above).
- **τί ἢ δέ (170)**: kept "why indeed". The edition's ἢ δέ cannot be settled from the grammar; the note already says the particles are hard to pin down and that they sharpen the question, and neither layer pins them further.
- **Supplied verb at 165**: kept "and who has close-fighting attendants". The published 16.272 reads the nominative as "we", which the speaker there is; Glaucus has no "we", and the Greek leaves the verb out, so a supplied "has" (with Achilles as the possessor) is the least that makes a sentence. The note says the verb is left out.
- **Βίη periphrasis (187)**: "the might of Patroclus" kept in both layers; the table has Πριάμοιο βίην "the might of Priam" and βίη Ἡρακληείη "the might of Heracles".
- **κυσί feminine (127)**: right. κύων is of common gender and Τρῳῇσιν is a feminine dative plural; the note's statement is true of the line.
- **φύξηλιν (143)**: "runaway" kept with the note that the word is rare and its shade not known; "coward" is reserved for κακός and would decide the shade.
- **δίωνται lemma (110)**: δίεμαι (subjunctive δίωμαι, 3 pl. δίωνται) is the right lemma for the "chase off" sense; no κε needed in a general simile.

## Considered and refused

- **ἀμφὶ … σάκος εὐρὺ καλύψας (132), "having spread"**: καλύπτω is "cover", and the table's ἀμφικαλύπτω "enfold" does not fit because the dative Μενοιτιάδῃ makes ἀμφί a preposition, not a preverb. "Having spread … about" is a fair reading of a shield held over a man; the note states the construction. Left.
- **χαλεπῷ μύθῳ (141) "harsh"**: the table shows both "hard" (5.384) and "harsh … reserved for χαλεπός" (the row at line 204 of conventions.md); the second is the stated reservation, so "harsh" stays.
- **θεσπέσιον "wondrous"** kept; **κακός "base"** in `l` and "coward" in `i` follows the table's note on κακός/κάκ’ ἐλέγχεα and the note on the line.
- **δαΐφρων (123)**: "wise-minded"/"wise-hearted" exactly as the table; note states the doubt.
- **ἐκέκλετο (183)** "gave orders": the table's ἐκέκλετο μακρὸν ἀΰσας row, unchanged.
- **Unit 169 note** ("a formula for a reply with the speaker's name changed; the line with Hector is also 12.230"): true, only awkwardly put; unchanged.
- **ὁτὲ δ’ (178)**: the departure from the published 16.690 (ὅτε conjunction) is right for the accent as printed; the note says so.
- **οὗτος (160)** as Patroclus and **αὐτόν (163)** as Sarpedon: the grammar and the exchange of bodies support the note; `i`'s "the man himself" follows "Sarpedon’s fine gear" and reads as Sarpedon.
- **Quotation marks**: “ on 120, 142, 170, 184; ” on 122, 168, 182, 187; `mark` on exactly those four units; `p` on 106, 123, 140, 169, 183, 188 matches the packet's paragraph marks. 183 (narrative between Hector's two speeches) has no quotes, correctly. No change.
- **Remembered English**: nothing found that arrived whole; the similes (108–112, 132–136) are rebuilt from the Greek.

## Counts
Moderate 7 (112 valiant; 118 flight; 120 περ; 123 label; 143; 149; 186), minor 8 (listed above), major 0. Nothing unresolved. Glossary (`gloss.json`) does not exist yet, so the parse check belongs to pass 2.

# Review, pass 2 — iliad-109 (gloss.json, and a last skim of units.json)

Method: each of the 54 novel keys and the 16 `__broaden__` keys was parsed against every line where the form occurs (`t`), then against `l`/`i`/`n`; every known form was checked against its existing entry (known-forms.json equals the repo-root `iliad-glossary.json` entry for every key); every old entry inside `__broaden__` was compared with the root glossary (all 16 are the old entry whole, followed by " · "); novel entries are all under 230 characters, use ’ only, and carry no line numbers or "here". `t` untouched.

## Changes

| Key | Severity | Was wrong | Done |

| πεφήσεται (new `__broaden__`) | moderate | The glossary entry is φένω "will be slain"; units.json (pass 1) takes the form as a future passive of φαίνω, "will be shown", with ὄλεθρος as subject. The known entry did not cover this use | broadened: old entry whole + " · also φαίνω (derivation uncertain) — show; fut. pass. 3 sg. … ’will be shown, will appear’" |
| ἔθεντο (new `__broaden__`) | minor | Entry has only "made for themselves"; πόνον καὶ δῆριν ἔθεντο ἀνδράσι is "laid toil and strife upon" | broadened with the + dat. reading |
| κλέος (`__broaden__`) | moderate | New reading called κλέος at the end of μέγα κλέος ἔμμεναι the "subject of an infinitive"; it is the predicate (the armour is the understood subject) | "predicate of ἔμμεναι" |

| ἔρριγα, μάχην (`__broaden__`) | minor | "shrink from" against "shudder at" in `l`/`i`/`n`; the root glossary has ἔρριγ’ "shudder, shrink from" | ἔρριγα: "shudder, shrink from (+ acc.) … ’I shudder at’"; μάχην: ’shudder at battle’ |

## Checked and left

- δίωνται ← δίεμαι (pres. subj. mid. 3 pl.), φύξηλιν (adj. of two endings, acc. sg., with σ’), μετασπών ← μεθέπω (aor. part., root σπ-), ἀνεχάζεθ’ ← ἀναχάζομαι (impf. mid., elided), ἔρριγα ← ῥιγέω (perf., present sense), Τρῳῇσιν (fem. dat. pl. of Τρῳός, with κυσί): all true of the line(s).
- σαώσῃς (subj., indirect question 144) and σαώσειας (opt., potential 149) kept apart; σπεύσομεν as "fut. (or short-vowel aor. subj.)" hortative matches the note; σχήσω fut. (179); ἐτάλασσας "aor. 2 sg." (second person) as ἔτλης.
- Known forms whose entries already cover this part and need no broadening: ὄφρ’ (already has "until"/"while" + ἄν + subj.), ἂν, δύω (aor. subj. "put on" after ὄφρ’ ἂν), ἢ (τί ἢ δέ "why then"), ᾧ/ἃ/οἷσι (possessive readings present), τὰ (article-like), οἷον (exclamatory), περί (+ gen. "for the sake of"; adv. "beyond others"), ἐπ’ + dat. "against", κατ’ ὄσσε, ἀμφί + dat., γενέσθαι, τίς/τις, κε (+ subj. / + opt.), μάχεσθαι (after a verb of urging).
- δυσμενέεσσι: entry reads "hostile … (also as noun)"; the form is an adjective with ἀνδράσι, and the entry is true of that.
- The `__broaden__` additions for βεβήκει, δῦνε, μάχης, οἷόν, τέ, ἀϋτῇ, ἐριβώλακα, ἐρυσαίμεθα, ἐρυσσάμενος, ἔλθοι, ἴδε, ὥς, αἶψά were each checked against the line(s) and are true.
- Re-skim of units.json: no residue from pass 1’s edits found (`l`/`i`/`n` agree on 112, 118, 120–121, 143, 149–151, 155, 170, 186, 188; `t`, marks and `p` flags unchanged).

## Counts
Moderate 3 (πεφήσεται, κλέος, ἐνείη), minor 4 (ἔθεντο, ἔρριγα/μάχην, πολυδακρύου, 142 `i`), major 0. Nothing unresolved; no refusals beyond the items under "Checked and left".
